boy1: Woken up with a stiff neck and can’t turn your head? What causes wry neck, how long does it last and what helps? Warning signs and six exercises to do at home.
boy3: Woke up unable to turn your head, as if your neck were locked to one side? Wry neck is a sudden spasm of the muscles on one side of the neck that leaves the head tilted and turned to one side. It can be very painful and frightening, but it usually gets better on its own within a few days. Slow, regular movement is the best way to help it recover.

boy30: Start the movements slowly and small, and widen them a little each day. A mild stretch is normal; do not push into pain. Stop the exercise if you get pain spreading to the arm or numbness.
boy32: Sit upright and keep your shoulders still. Slowly turn your head to one side as far as the pain allows, hold for 2–3 seconds, then turn to the other side. Try to look a little further each day.

boy41: How long does wry neck last?
boy42: It usually gets better within a few days. The muscle spasm often eases in 24–48 hours, while full recovery can take up to a week. Sometimes it lasts longer or comes back later for no clear reason.
boy43: Will moving my neck harm it?
boy44: No. Moving the neck gently will not damage it; in fact, increasing the movement day by day supports recovery. If the pain is very bad, you can rest for a day or so and then start moving gently.
boy46: Heat eases muscle stiffness for many people. To avoid burning your skin, you can wrap the heat pack in a towel.
boy47: Should I wear a neck collar?
boy48: Usually not. The advice is to move the neck gradually and carry on with your daily activities as far as possible. Taking painkillers regularly, before the pain becomes severe, can make the exercises easier.
